4756307055294781279:
A painter once acquired ancient scroll fragments depicting landscapes and cities, their figures lifelike. Obsessed with copying them, he began noticing ink stains seeping into reality around him, voices reciting theatrical lines.
One night, as the oil lamp flickered, he saw fresh ink bleeding from the paper’s edge onto his walls. In panic, he dipped his brush and added a stroke to "his" corner. Instantly, the world spun—walls crumpled like Xuan paper, revealing scroll rods and canvas beyond.
He realized then: he and his world were but drying ink on a vast painting. A whisper came from beyond: "This stroke… was unnecessary." With those words, the painter and his hut vanished, leaving only a fresh, insignificant blot on the ancient scroll.
